L1.en: In the court of Ayodhyā, the sage sat before the king.
L1.hi: अयोध्या के दरबार में ऋषि विश्वामित्र राजा के सामने बैठे थे।
L1.te: అయోధ్య సభలో విశ్వామిత్రుడు రాజు ముందు కూర్చున్నాడు.
L1.evidence: the audience is Dutt XIX; the seating is inferred

L2.en: And Dasharatha had already given his word.
L2.hi: और दशरथ वचन दे चुके थे — ऋषि जो माँगेंगे, वो देंगे।
L2.te: దశరథుడు అప్పటికే మాట ఇచ్చేశాడు — ఋషి ఏం అడిగినా ఇస్తానని.

L3.en: Before he asked, the sage told him: keep your word.
L3.hi: माँगने से पहले ऋषि ने कहा — अपना वचन निभाना।
L3.te: అడిగే ముందే ఋషి అన్నాడు — మాట నిలబెట్టుకో.
L3.speaker: VISHVAMITRA
L3.evidence: CLM-0009, 18.3; Dutt XIX "prove firm in promise"
L3.speaker_rule: VISHVAMITRA's statement, not narrator fact. Attributed in every language.

L4.en: Far from here, in the forest, Viśvāmitra had begun a yajña.
L4.hi: दूर, जंगल में, विश्वामित्र ने एक यज्ञ शुरू किया था।
L4.te: ఇక్కడికి దూరంగా, అడవిలో, విశ్వామిత్రుడు ఒక యజ్ఞం మొదలుపెట్టాడు.

L5.en: Two rākṣasas kept breaking it. Mārīca. Subāhu.
L5.hi: दो राक्षस उसे बार-बार तोड़ देते थे। मारीच। सुबाहु।
L5.te: ఇద్దరు రాక్షసులు దాన్ని పదే పదే పాడు చేసేవారు. మారీచుడు. సుబాహుడు.

L6.en: They poured flesh and blood over the altar.
L6.hi: वो वेदी पर माँस और ख़ून उँडेल देते थे।

L7.en: He was under a vow. He couldn't curse them.
L7.hi: ऋषि व्रत में थे। शाप दे नहीं सकते थे।

L8.en: So he had come to the king.
L8.hi: इसलिए वो राजा के पास आए थे।
L8.evidence: 18.6–8 — he is there, stating his need

L9.en: Ten nights. That was all he asked.
L9.hi: दस रातें। बस इतना ही माँगा था।

L10.en: He did not ask for the army.
L10.evidence: true by omission: 18.8 asks for Rāma, not an army

screenplay.en: In the court of Ayodhyā, the sage sat before the king.
And Dasharatha had already given his word.
Before he asked, the sage told him: keep your word.
Far from here, in the forest, Viśvāmitra had begun a yajña.
Two rākṣasas kept breaking it. Mārīca. Subāhu.
They poured flesh and blood over the altar.
He was under a vow. He couldn't curse them.
So he had come to the king.
Ten nights. That was all he asked.
He did not ask for the army.

sound.design: Room tone and one lamp. A low drone, barely audible, enters at beat 4 and is **gone by beat 15** — the reveal is dry. No reverb on the name. No musical hit.
sound.room_tone: continues across a continuous join; never reseated

cues.cue: A low drone, barely audible, enters at beat 4 and is gone by beat 15 — the reveal is dry.

hero_frame.why: The one frame holding both the promise and the price. A stranger sees an old king told something he cannot undo.
hero_frame.use: poster, share card, and the frame a stranger sees first

continuity._what: What must not change between cuts.
standing_rules: The lamp stays where it is. Its flame moves; its position does not.
Daśaratha's ring is on the right hand in every hand detail, in every film.
The throne is occupied in films 1–2 and empty from film 3 onward. It is never re-occupied.
Viśvāmitra's staff is planted at his right through films 1–4. It moves once, in film 5.
The sage's cloth and seated posture do not change across four films — that stillness is the performance and a shifted fold breaks it.
Once the king steps down in film 3, he does not return to the dais in any later shot.

per_join.continuous: The frame is IDENTICAL across the join — same plate, same grade, same room tone. Not a similar frame: the same one.
per_join.hard: Location or time has changed. Room tone changes with it.

never: Do not show the altar, the rite, or the rākṣasas. All three are spoken of and none is seen.
Do not cut to Rāma on his name. The scene is about his father.
Do not let the voice rise on the reveal.
Do not animate the sage's mouth as though he narrates. The storyteller narrates.

The king's stillness in the hold is GROUNDED in 19.1 — "for a moment as if senseless". Its 8-second length is a creative proposal, not the text's. Before it, the source has him lurch from his seat in fear (18.20). Render a small involuntary movement on the name, then the frozen face. Do not suppress the lurch; do not turn it into a faint.
Do not make the sage sinister at any point.
